findings.reason: The protected Python solution computes Stirling numbers of the second kind S(n, k) mod 10^9 + 7 to find the number of ways to distribute n distinct candies into k unlabeled non-empty bags. It uses space-optimized 1D dynamic programming with inner loop iterating backwards over bags from min(candies, k) down to 1. The solution runs in O(n * k) time and O(k) space; no candidate is required.
Backward iteration over bags ensures DP states from candies - 1 are read before being updated, correctly computing S(i, j) = S(i - 1, j - 1) + j * S(i - 1, j) mod 10^9 + 7.
Outer loop iterates n times and inner loop iterates min(i, k) <= k times, yielding O(n * k) time. 1D DP array of size k + 1 requires O(k) space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts integers n and k, returning the number of valid distributions modulo 10^9 + 7.

The approach accurately details Stirling numbers of the second kind recurrence, backward 1D DP array state updates, and O(n * k) time / O(k) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover 2D DP table space usage, labeled-bag overcounting traps, stars and bars misapplication, repeated addition overhead, single bag boundary cases, one candy per bag boundary cases, and intermediate modulo reduction.

App Python and native Python solutions both execute the identical Stirling numbers 1D DP algorithm with SHA-256 digests 857de7ea15326464be66a206a04d20c4f6bb508b392cb400611ed06f0da34229 and c98ce0a0f381661862635131ce665f20688ff5d632d4f8420cb88129b5e677c7. Verified submission remains untouched.

Statement structure and factual evidence confirmed n and k interface, three examples, one constraint, and 0 diagrams. Bound to content SHA-256 b8225c9bb6f57ea5427a83f10806bd0781c93957e50b2bfd502d9118c30bbb28.
